column80.enabled.description: Show tab completion suggestions from a local model as you type. On by default. Needs the tab completion model (offered on first run) and a running Ollama server; without them no suggestion appears. Dictation works with this off.

column80.fimUsageExamples.description: At a member call whose name you have typed, show the model how your workspace already calls that member, found through your language server. Fewer suggestions fail to compile. Adds at most 50ms to a suggestion. In C# it rarely helps, because the lookup usually takes longer than that.

column80.fimLanguages.description: Extra languages to offer tab completion in, by VS Code language id ('cpp', not '.cpp'). Column 80 already covers Rust, C#, Python, Go, TypeScript and JavaScript. Use this for C, C++, Java, Kotlin and the like. It also gates dictation on a code line, the take that becomes a suggestion. Dictating into a comment, or into a markdown or plain text file, needs no entry here, and adding markdown turns on tab completion in markdown. In a language whose comment syntax Column 80 does not know (zig, f#, ocaml and similar), suggestions can appear inside comments.

column80.apiBase.description: Base URL of the Ollama server that serves function generation. Point it at another machine to run the big model there. Tab completion always runs locally and ignores this when it names another machine.

column80.fimModel.description: Ollama model for tab completion. Must be a base model that supports fill-in-the-middle, not an -instruct model.

column80.fnGenModel.description: Model for per-function generation. An instruct/chat model. For the local (ollama) backend this is an ollama tag; for a cloud provider set it to that provider's model id (e.g. an OpenAI, Claude, Grok, or Gemini id from their docs).

column80.fnGenThinking.markdownDescription:
Reasoning mode for the generation model. **Leave it empty.** Empty means the hardware tier decides, and every tier that ships a reasoning model turns reasoning off. In testing on twelve C# functions, reasoning compiled no more of them and took about ten times as long.

Ollama and the OpenAI-compatible backends receive it. Anthropic and Claude Code ignore it.

- *(empty)*: the hardware tier decides.
- `off`: turn reasoning off explicitly.
- `on`: turn reasoning on. Expect about ten times the wait, and most answers cut off before the code is written.
- anything else (`low`, `medium`, `high`, …): passed to the model as written. If the model refuses it, the output channel shows the model's own message.

column80.fnGenProvider.description: Backend for per-function generation. 'ollama' is the default: local, offline, first. The others send your prompt (signature, doc comment, selected context and the type definitions Column 80 looked up) off the machine: 'claude-code' through your installed Claude Code CLI on your subscription, the rest to a cloud model over an OpenAI-compatible API with an API key. Tab completion always runs locally.
enumDescriptions: Local ollama. Offline after the one-time model pull. The default.

Claude Code. Runs your installed claude CLI and bills your Claude subscription, no API key. Your code leaves the machine. Set fnGenModel to a Claude model id, or leave it at the ollama default and the CLI picks its own. Tab completion stays local.
OpenAI. Needs cloudApiKey and an OpenAI model id in fnGenModel.

Anthropic (Claude), over its native Messages API. Needs cloudApiKey and a Claude model id in fnGenModel. This is the one cloud provider that can cache your context blocks: one breakpoint is placed after them, with a one-hour lifetime, so a second generation against the same blocks reads them instead of re-sending them.
xAI (Grok). Needs cloudApiKey and a Grok model id in fnGenModel.
Google (Gemini), via its OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Needs cloudApiKey and a Gemini model id in fnGenModel.
Any other OpenAI-compatible server (OpenRouter, Groq, DeepSeek, a local vLLM). Needs cloudApiBase and usually cloudApiKey.

column80.cloudApiKey.description: API key for the cloud fnGenProvider. Sent as a Bearer token, except on 'anthropic', whose native API takes it as x-api-key. Ignored by the local 'ollama' backend and by 'claude-code', which authenticates through the CLI's own subscription login. Leave it empty and function generation stays off with a message.

column80.cloudApiBase.description: Endpoint override for the cloud backend. Required for the 'openai-compatible' provider (the full base URL up to /chat/completions, e.g. https://openrouter.ai/api/v1). Optional for the named providers, whose base URL is built in; set it only to point at a proxy or a moved host. On 'anthropic' it is the root /messages hangs off. Ignored by 'claude-code', which has no endpoint.

column80.fnGenFallbackModel.description: Function-generation model for the 16gb-low-ram tier (a dense model of about 9GB that fits on the GPU whole).

column80.hardwareTier.description: Hardware tier: decides which models run and how they share GPU memory. 'auto' probes VRAM and RAM on activation; a tier id overrides the probe.
enumDescriptions: Probe nvidia-smi and system RAM, pick the tier automatically.
24GB+ VRAM: both models run fully on the GPU (untested).
16GB VRAM, 32GB+ RAM: the 30B generation model, partly on the GPU, beside the tab completion model.
12-16GB VRAM or low RAM: a smaller 14B generation model.
Below 12GB or no GPU: tab completion only, function generation disabled.

column80.maxTokens.description: Longest tab completion suggestion, in tokens.

column80.temperature.description: Sampling temperature. Low values keep completions stable.

column80.debounceMs.description: Delay after the last keystroke before requesting a completion. 0 turns the delay off, so every keystroke asks the language server and the model; that is expensive on a busy machine. Negative values are refused.

column80.prefixChars.description: Characters of context kept before the cursor. The minimum is 10; fewer can cut off the member name you are typing.

column80.suffixChars.description: Characters of context kept after the cursor.

column80.cacheCapacity.description: Tab completion suggestions kept for reuse. 0 turns the cache off, so every keystroke asks the model, which is slower.

column80.minGhostChars.description: Shortest suggestion worth showing, in characters. JetBrains' full-line completion uses 8: a three-character suggestion costs a full review for almost nothing. A suggestion that ends on a block opener is never refused on length. Set to 0 to show every suggestion.

column80.minGhostAlnum.description: Letters and digits a suggestion must carry to be shown, so pure punctuation like ");" is never offered. JetBrains uses the same number. Set to 0 to judge length alone.

column80.repairEnabled.description: Let the function-generation model repair compiler errors, up to two rounds through the normal preview, after an accepted generation and when you run Repair Function Body. Off: the errors are shown and nothing is repaired, and Repair Function Body does not run covering tests or compare the function with how the rest of the repo uses what it calls.

column80.repairUsageWindows.description: Show the model how your code already calls what a failing function calls, during repair. Off by default: in testing it repaired no more functions and made each repair round about 2.6s slower.

column80.compilerDirectedInjection.description: Look up the real methods of the types your code names, through your language server, and show them to the model so it calls methods that exist. Applies to Generate Function Body and Repair Function Body in Rust, C#, Python, Go and TypeScript. Off: repair sees only the compiler errors.

column80.fimAlternatives.description: Suggestions generated when you trigger inline suggestions by hand (Alt+\). Cycle them with Alt+] and Alt+[. Typing always generates one, to stay fast. Duplicates are dropped, so you may see fewer. Nothing shows until the slowest one finishes, and if Ollama runs one request at a time, expect roughly this many times the wait.

column80.fimMemberGate.description: Hide ghost text after a "." when the member it names does not exist on that type (Rust, C#, Python, Go and TypeScript, and only when the language server lists the type's members; untyped values and index-signature types are never filtered). Turn off if it hides suggestions you wanted; the output channel logs every one it hides.

column80.logPrompts.description: Debug: write the full prompt to the output channel on every function generation, repair round and tab completion, between prompt-begin/prompt-end markers. Shows exactly what the model was given, including the type information Column 80 added. Tab completion asks on every keystroke, so this is very verbose; leave it off for normal use.

column80.injectedContext.description: How much of your code Column 80 shows the model when it generates or repairs a function. Match it to the model: small for a local 30B, frontier for Opus-class cloud models. Higher means a bigger prompt and a slower first answer. The output channel says what each generation included.
enumDescriptions: For a 30B-class local model. The default: a small model can do worse when the prompt runs long.
For a 30B with room to spend: a bigger card, or a quantization that leaves headroom.
For a large local model, or a cheap cloud one.
For Opus and Fable class models. Shows the model as much of your code as Column 80 can look up.

column80.dictation.enabled.markdownDescription: Dictation: press the shortcut, speak, press it again. On a code line Column 80 writes the code from what it heard. Inside a comment the words become the comment. In a markdown or plain text file the words go in as you said them. Off stops the speech recogniser, which runs on this machine and never in the cloud.

column80.dictation.microphone.markdownDescription: The capture device dictation records from, by the exact name `Column 80: Select Microphone` lists. Empty means the system default.

column80.dictation.muteSpeakers.markdownDescription: Mute the speakers while the microphone is open, and put them back as they were. Music bleeds into the transcript otherwise. Linux (wpctl or pactl) and macOS today; Windows is not muted yet.

column80.dictation.partials.markdownDescription: Show what is being heard on the cursor line while you talk, updated every 300ms. Off shows only the recording pulse until you stop.

column80.dictation.surfaces.markdownDescription: Look up the type names you spoke through the language server and show their definitions to the model above your comment. Off skips the lookup.

column80.dictation.autoAccept.markdownDescription: Put the generated code straight into the file when it lands and drop the cursor to the next line, with nothing pressed. Off leaves it as a suggestion for Tab or Escape.

enumDescriptions: Shift+Alt+D (shadows VS Code's Detect Language from Content)
Shift+Alt+M
Shift+Alt+Space
Ctrl+Shift+Alt+D
F9 (VS Code's Toggle Breakpoint; only pick this if you never use it)
No default chord; bind column80.dictate yourself in Keyboard Shortcuts
column80.dictation.shortcut.markdownDescription: The chord that toggles dictation. Pick one here, or `none` and bind `column80.dictate` to anything in the Keyboard Shortcuts editor. Ctrl+Alt chords are not offered: that is AltGr on many Windows layouts. Escape cancels a take at any point (`column80.cancelDictation`).
